lore.skyabyss.prologue.the_book.title: Blank Notebook
lore.skyabyss.prologue.the_book.inscript:
Write it down before you forget.
Next time, notice sooner.
lore.skyabyss.prologue.the_book.body:
That was all, on the first page, in a hand I don't recognise. The other pages are blank.

An old notebook. The cover is cold as stone and worn at the corners. I can't quite remember where I got it.
lore.skyabyss.prologue.shadow.title: Shadow Overhead
lore.skyabyss.prologue.shadow.body:
At noon on a clear day, everything went dark. Something was crossing above the clouds. Its shadow covered a whole hill.

The sheep lay down. The birds went quiet. Then a low sound came down, like wings beating the air.

I started to write what I saw through the clouds, and stopped.
lore.skyabyss.prologue.counting_song.ins:
One, at noon the shadow comes.
Two, lie down beside the sheep.
Three, and don't you look up.
Four, at night the moon comes.
lore.skyabyss.prologue.counting_song.bod:
Village children sing it while bouncing a ball. Nobody knows what comes after four.

When I asked the grown-ups, they changed the subject.
lore.skyabyss.prologue.seventh_night.ins: On the seventh night, bar the door and stay inside.
lore.skyabyss.prologue.seventh_night.bod:
The same line was written in the margin of an old almanac, once every seven days.

The village says it has always been the rule. Nobody knows why the seventh.
lore.skyabyss.prologue.shaved_peak.title: Flattened Peak
lore.skyabyss.prologue.shaved_peak.body:
One morning the top of the northern peak was gone. So the shepherd says.

It didn't fall, he says. It was flat, as if scraped off from above, and the cut rock was still pale.
lore.skyabyss.prologue.watcher.title: The Watcher
lore.skyabyss.prologue.watcher.body:
Keeping the fire alone at night, you may see someone standing a long way off.

Call out and they are gone. Walk over and there are no footprints.

The old folk call it the Watcher. Don't meet its eyes, they say, and it does nothing.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.stone_whale.title: The Stone Whale
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.stone_whale.body:
A long, low song came from across the sky.

A mountain of rock was swimming under the clouds, ruins lined along its back. It turned slowly, its whole body bending.

I couldn't tell if it had eyes. I felt watched all the same.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.sky_ruins.title: Ruins on Its Back
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.sky_ruins.body:
The chain hauled me up into a town. Or what had been one.

The paving is cracked, the pillars are down, and only a gate of bone still stands. No one is here.

Stand still and the stones lift you a little, then set you down. This is not the ground.
On the ledge of the goal, past the western chasm.

A pilgrim road, but it never says to where.

With my ear to the stone, I heard a low hum.
Beside the goal in the captain's hall.

It speaks of a return. The sentinels turned to bone before that day came.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.inscription_below:
On the wall of the little room past the dark waterway.

Why would a creature with no breath sing? Underwater, listening, I could tell the beat came from below.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.inscription_vault:
On the corridor wall, beyond the seal.

Beside the words one who remains is a row of thin scratches, as if made with a fingernail. I counted seven.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.inscription_heart:
On the wall of the anteroom, before the heart's chamber.

Beyond the door something is beating. If it isn't the titan's, where is its owner?
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.captain.title: Whalebone Captain
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.captain.body:
The captain never lowered its pike, not until it fell apart.

In the heap of bone lay a worn clasp. On the front, the mark of the people of the back. On the reverse, small, something like a name. I could only read the first letter.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.heart_stilled.bod:
The stone whale's heart stopped. The titan did not fall. It only let out one deep breath.

I stood a while in the quiet chamber. The stone walls were still warm.

Where did that beat come from, and where has it gone?
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.sky_key.title: Sky Key Fragment
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.sky_key.body:
When the heart stopped, there was a fragment in my hand. Faintly warm. It pulses, just barely.

Four of them, the old stories say, open a door above the clouds. The other three must lie deep inside the other titans.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.carried_people.bo:
The people of the back called themselves the Carried, it seems.

They owned no land. Born on the titan's back, they died there too. Their dead were laid along the road until the bones became the road.

I thought of the bone road in the west.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.return_fire.title: Returning Fire
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.return_fire.body:
The fires at the resting places burn blue. No one feeds them, and they have never gone out.

The people called it the returning fire. Whoever falls on the back wakes up beside it.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.whale_song.title: The Whale's Song
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.whale_song.body:
The stone whale sings, the page says, only before it comes down below the clouds.

The people took the song as a sign that someone was being fetched. Who, I can't read. The page is torn there.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.whale_chaser.body:
The traveller who keeps a fire at the edge of the village called himself Isana. In an old tongue, they say, it means whale.

He paused a moment before he said it, like someone who had told the same name to someone before.

The next time we meet, will he remember?
lore.skyabyss.prologue.camp.title: The Travelers' Camp
lore.skyabyss.prologue.camp.body:
The fire had gone cold, nothing left but its ring of stones. The cart lay on its side, and the bedroll gaped open, still hollowed in the shape of a person.

Most of the baggage was gone. Only the notebook had been left behind. There was not a single footprint in the grass from whoever took it.

Who spent the night here?
lore.skyabyss.prologue.the_book_margin.b:
I cannot tell when it was written. The margin was blank last night.

The handwriting matches the line on the first page.

Who keeps writing ahead of me?
lore.skyabyss.prologue.footprints.title: Giant Footprints
lore.skyabyss.prologue.footprints.body:
A little off the road, hollows in the shape of feet lay in the ground, three of them, evenly spaced. Their floors were hard stone, and rainwater had gathered in them.

One step, and a house would sink.

I could find no trace of them before or behind. Where was the one who walked here headed?
lore.skyabyss.prologue.footsteps.title: Night Footsteps
lore.skyabyss.prologue.footsteps.body:
Not long after sundown, the insects fell silent. The wind stopped too.

The ground shook three times, slowly, each stronger than the last, and then faded into the distance.

I could see nothing in the dark. Even so, I knew something had passed.

What was walking?
lore.skyabyss.prologue.bone_hill.title: The Bone Hill
lore.skyabyss.prologue.bone_hill.body:
On a hill stood a gigantic rib cage, arching up from the ground, polished stone-white by long years of wind. I tried to count the ribs and gave up partway.

A single line was carved into the slab at its foot.

Can something this vast really end?
lore.skyabyss.prologue.sky_song.title: The Song from the Sky
lore.skyabyss.prologue.sky_song.body:
At night, a song came down from the sky. A low, long voice, with no way to tell where it came from.

The stars went out in a broad band, as if something were passing high above. When the song ended, the stars returned as though nothing had happened.

What was it that hid the stars?
